directions.title: NET-61: CONTENT-ADDITIVE-EVICTION-DOES-NOT-HELP — hybrid z(acc)+lambda*z(probe) monotonically worse with probe weight; all four cheap signal families bounded >=5.7pts below oracle
directions.description:
## NET-61 — limited-memory axis, round 14 (paper 146, ResearchOutput/exp_net61_hybrid.py, /tmp/net61.log)

**Verdict name: CONTENT-ADDITIVE-EVICTION-DOES-NOT-HELP.**

### Result
Hybrid eviction score = z(accumulated usage) + λ·z(static probe score), Qwen2.5-0.5B ctx=1024 (gate exact 1.0000; probes train-side):

| B | λ | retained |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | **0.0** | **0.9384** |
| 64 | 0.25 | 0.9383 |
| 64 | 1.0 | 0.9365 |
| 64 | 4.0 | 0.9344 |
| 32 | 1.0 | 0.9189 |
| 128 | 1.0 | 0.9544 |

- **P1 REFUTED**: no λ > 0 beats λ = 0 — the response is monotonically DECREASING in probe weight.
- **P2 CONFIRMED**: λ = 0 is optimal.
- **P3 CONFIRMED**: best hybrid trails oracle@64 by 5.7 points.

Consistency anchor: the λ=0 arm reproduces NET-56's hybrid to FOUR DECIMALS (0.9384).

### The law
With NET-56 (accumulation), NET-58 (content alone), and now content-additive hybrids, every cheap eviction-signal family is bounded ≥5.7 pts below oracle at matched budget: **the policy gap is robust to accumulation, recency, content, and their linear combinations.** Remaining routes are structural (usage-tracking quality, learned online predictors at scale — themselves bounded by NET-58's weak-probe ceiling) or accepting oracle-only claims as upper bounds.

### All 8 barriers
(a) clean — three horns pre-stated incl. the refuted P1; (b) confronted — score-combination hybrids exist in H2O variants; NEW = the measured monotone-degradation law + four-family bounding of the gap; (c) confronted — one model/context, linear probes, fixed recency window; (d) clean — train-side probes; (e) deterministic, λ-grid pre-stated; (f) clean — ALL_DONE_NET61; (g) fair — identical harness/budgets/windows as NET-56/58; (h) DIRECT.

### Next
Sub-16 addendum @1024 (running next); domain-jump corpora; 1.5B tail map; 7B quantized-offload cell.

Now 61 network experiments. Assessment v61. Paper 146.

directions.title: Kneser input for many lines
directions.description:
*Let `v_1, …, v_k` be pairwise independent
   directions in `F_p²` and `S_i ⊆ F_p` with `0 ∈ S_i`.  If
   `Σ_i (p - |S_i|) ≤ (k-2)(p-1)`, then `Σ_i S_i v_i = F_p²`.*  The case
   `k = 3` is proved here (`Heis.exists_triple_solution`, in the sharper form
   `Σ_i (p-|S_i|) < p`); the general statement would immediately give a
   `k`-auxiliary-class spread exclusion and, at `p = 5`, would remove the
   profile `(8,2,2,2,2,2)`.

directions.title: NET-60: THE-EPISTASIS-LIVES-IN-THE-TAIL-PAIR — L22+L23 solo costs sum to 0.06pts but joint pruning costs 0.42pts (7x super-additive); the last two layers are one coordinated unit
directions.description:
## NET-60 — limited-memory axis, round 13 (paper 145, ResearchOutput/exp_net60_pairs.py, /tmp/net60.log)

**Verdict name: THE-EPISTASIS-LIVES-IN-THE-TAIL-PAIR.**

### Result
Six pair/triple ablations at k=16/layer (Qwen2.5-0.5B, ctx=512), each cost compared to the sum of its members' NET-59 solo costs:

| arm | layers | retained | cost | Σsolo | class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **tail_22_23** | 22,23 | 0.9958 | **0.42 pts** | **0.06** | **SUPER 7×** |
| bulk_12_15 | 12,15 | 0.9940 | 0.60 | 0.79 | sub |
| front_0_1 | 0,1 | 0.9975 | 0.25 | 0.25 | ≈additive |
| mid_10_11 | 10,11 | 0.9960 | 0.40 | 0.28 | super 1.4× |
| cross_22_12 | 22,12 | 0.9941 | 0.59 | 0.60 | sub |
| **triple_21_22_23** | 21,22,23 | 0.9924 | **0.76** | **0.19** | **SUPER 4×** |

- **P1 CONFIRMED**: the tail pair is simultaneously the cheapest by solo sum and disproportionately costly jointly — 7× super-additive.
- **P2 REFUTED**: three of six arms are super-additive.
- **P3 CONFIRMED**: the tail triple compounds at 4× and is the most costly arm.

### The law
The last two layers function as a COORDINATED UNIT — co-adapted during pretraining; sparsifying either alone is absorbed, degrading both removes a joint capability no other pair exhibits. This causal signature matches the four correlational markers (NET-50 far-from-tropical, crystallization loss, NET-51 decision divergence, NET-54 unportability). **Prescription: treat the tail as ONE unit for bits/budgets — never differentiate between its members.**

### All 8 barriers
(a) clean — three horns pre-stated incl. the refuted P2; (b) clean — pairwise super-additivity maps for pretrained LLM attention not previously measured; (c) confronted — one context/model, k=16 granularity, five chosen pairs stated; (d) clean — held-out, no training; (e) deterministic, solo sums inherited from the committed NET-59 profile; (f) clean — ALL_DONE_NET60; (g) fair — identical budgets across arms; (h) DIRECT.

### Next
1.5B replication; deeper-tail units on larger models; probe+recency hybrid (NET-58 follow-up); domain-jump corpora.

Now 60 network experiments. Assessment v60. Paper 145.

directions.title: NET-68: CODE-NEEDS-FEWER-KEYS — domain jump to Python shifts the knee chain down one fine step ({12,16} vs {16,20}); budget law now domain-parameterized
directions.description:
## NET-68 — limited-memory axis, round 21 (paper 153, ResearchOutput/exp_net68_domainjump.py, /tmp/net68.log)

**Verdict name: CODE-NEEDS-FEWER-KEYS.**

### Result
Domain jump to Python source (10 CPython stdlib files; gate exact; identical harness/bar):

| ctx | code k\* | prose k\* | code full acc | shift |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | **12** | 16 | 0.6296 | −4 keys |
| 1024 | **16** | 20 | 0.6520 | −4 keys |

Code sweeps @512: 4: 0.930 ✗, 8: 0.969 ✗, **12: 0.981 ✓**, 16: 0.987, 20: 0.988, 24: 0.989.
@1024: 8: 0.960 ✗, 12: 0.976 ✗, **16: 0.981 ✓**, 20: 0.986, 24: 0.987.

- **P1 CONFIRMED**: knees transfer within one fine step.
- **P2 CONFIRMED**: exactly one fine-grid step (−4 keys) below prose at BOTH contexts — structure preserved.
- **P3 REFUTED**.

### The parameterized budget law
k\*(domain, context) = base(domain) + increment(scale) × doublings(context), with base(prose)=16, base(code)=12, increments set by scale (NET-67). THIRD independent confirmation that accuracy level and knee position are independent quantities: code is EASIER to predict yet needs FEWER keys. Deployment: size KV by the largest-base domain present in mixed workloads.

### All 8 barriers
(a) clean — three horns pre-stated incl. the refuted P3; (b) clean; (c) confronted — limits: ONE code language, single-repo source, 24 windows stated; (d) clean per-corpus held-out splits; (e) deterministic; (f) clean — ALL_DONE_NET68; (g) fair — byte-identical harness except text; (h) DIRECT.

### Next
Math/non-English domains; increments at 4096; probe+recency hybrid on code; 7B quantized-offload cell.

Now 68 network experiments. Assessment v68. Paper 153.

directions.title: NET-67: SCALE-HALVES-THE-CONTEXT-INCREMENT — 1.5B knee at 2048 is 18 not 20; both models start at 16 keys, scale halves the +per-doubling increment (+4 -> +2)
directions.description:
## NET-67 — limited-memory axis, round 20 (paper 152, ResearchOutput/exp_net67_sub20.py, /tmp/net67.log)

**Verdict name: SCALE-HALVES-THE-CONTEXT-INCREMENT.**

### Result
Two-point addendum (Qwen2.5-1.5B, ctx=2048; baseline drift-assert passed exactly 0.5132):

| k | 14 | 18 |
|---|---|---|
| retained | 0.9757 ✗ (~2 SE) | **0.9811 ✓** |

- **P1 CONFIRMED**: the knee is 18 — NET-66's coarse read of 20 was one fine point high.
- **P2 REFUTED** accordingly.

### The refined law
Complete measured picture: 0.5B {16, 20, 24} — starts at 16, +4 keys per context doubling. 1.5B {16, 16, 18} — starts at 16, +2 keys per doubling (first increment 0, second +2). **Scale compresses both the level and the increments of the attention-budget curve.** The one-octave reading (NET-66) was a coarse-grid approximation; increment-halving is the finer truth. Deployment: a 20-key budget covers BOTH models to 2048 with margin.

### All 8 barriers
(a) clean — two horns pre-stated incl. the refuted P2; (b) clean; (c) confronted — two-point addendum stated; (d) clean; (e) deterministic drift-assert; (f) clean — ALL_DONE_NET67; (g) fair — same bar; (h) DIRECT.

### Next
Increments at 4096; domain-jump corpora; 7B cell (does halving extend?).

Now 67 network experiments. Assessment v67. Paper 152.

directions.title: NET-65: SIXTEEN-IS-REAL — all sub-16 points fail on Qwen2.5-1.5B at ctx=1024 (knee exactly 16); scale flattens the context response: {16,20,24}@0.5B vs flat {16,16}@1.5B
directions.description:
## NET-65 — limited-memory axis, round 18 (paper 150, ResearchOutput/exp_net65_1p5bsub16.py, /tmp/net65.log)

**Verdict name: SIXTEEN-IS-REAL.**

### Result
Fine sweep below NET-55's grid floor (Qwen2.5-1.5B, ctx=1024, gate identical to NET-55; baseline bit-identical 0.5004):

| k | 4 | 6 | 8 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| retained | 0.9318 ✗ | 0.9532 ✗ | 0.9660 ✗ | **0.9759 ✗ (razor, ~2 SE)** |

- **P1 REFUTED**: no sub-16 point passes — the knee does NOT decline with scale.
- **P2 CONFIRMED**: k\*(1024) = 16 exact, bracket (12, 16].

### The refined scale law
0.5B: {16, 20, 24} — the chain RISES with context. 1.5B: {16, 16} — FLAT. Larger models have more context-STABLE attention budgets, not fewer keys. New measurable: the CONTEXT-SENSITIVITY of the attention budget, which decreases with model scale in its first measured step. A 16-key budget covers both models to ctx=1024.

### All 8 barriers
(a) clean; (b) clean; (c) confronted — razor bracket (12, 16] stated; one corpus; (d) clean; (e) deterministic baseline-replicating; (f) clean — ALL_DONE_NET65; (g) fair — same bar/harness as NET-55; (h) DIRECT.

### Next
1.5B @2048 fine grid (does the flat chain break upward?); domain-jump corpora; 7B cell.

Now 65 network experiments. Assessment v65. Paper 150.

directions.description:
## NET-64 — limited-memory axis, round 17 (paper 149, ResearchOutput/exp_net64_fine2048B.py, /tmp/net64.log)

**Verdict name: THE-CORPUS-B-DISAGREEMENT-WAS-A-GRID-ARTIFACT.**

### Result
Corpus-B fine sweep at ctx=2048 (gate exact):

| k | 20 | 24 | 28 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| retained | 0.9790 ✗ | **0.9832 ✓** | 0.9853 ✓ | 0.9862 ✓ |

**k\*(2048) = 24 — IDENTICAL to corpus-A's fine knee.**

- **P1 REFUTED**: no shard-level difference at long context — the fine knees match.
- **P2 CONFIRMED**: corpus-B's coarse-grid 32 was a grid artifact.
- **P3 REFUTED**: nothing "between".

### The completed chain
The full 0.5B fine-grid chain **{16, 20, 24} at {512, 1024, 2048} now replicates EXACTLY across two disjoint wikitext shards at every cell** — every entry of the deployment table is dual-corpus-confirmed. Baseline note: corpus-B acc 0.4946 vs A's 0.4760 (shard-2 text is easier) yet identical knees — accuracy level and knee position are independent.

### All 8 barriers
(a) clean — three horns pre-stated incl. two refuted; (b) clean; (c) confronted — 12 windows stated; (d) clean; (e) deterministic; (f) clean — ALL_DONE_NET63 marker (reused harness); (g) fair — byte-identical harness except corpus path; (h) DIRECT.
